dedupe_keys.name: tallinn multiscale building and urban heat geospatial data

description: This Mendeley deposit publishes geoprocessed urban data for 34,001 buildings across all eight districts of Tallinn, Estonia. Nasim Eslamirad assembled building locations and characteristics with urban, heat-island and climate variables to support analysis of urban heat. The repository describes an ascending hierarchical grid system that assigns objects a spatial index and connects heterogeneous source data to common spatial units. Python and QGIS were used to process the inputs. The dataset is freely accessible under CC BY 4.0. The inspected repository metadata does not identify a uniform observation period, grid-cell size or downloadable file format; those details require checking before model calibration. These are processed variables, so spatial association does not by itself establish a causal temperature response to a building intervention. A reviewer-assessed use is preparing exposure inputs or comparing alternative urban-form descriptions in heat-adaptation simulations. platform-qgis is the documented processing environment. The related GitHub code is separately reviewed, while a second Mendeley deposit contains article figures, not additional tabular observations.
